canonical_fact: A guarantor is a validator assigned to evaluate a work package, reconstruct its required data, execute it into a work report and sign a guarantee when correct.
title: Guarantor

canonical_fact: A guarantee is a signed validator attestation over a work report, submitted as block extrinsic data so the report can enter JAM's on-chain availability pipeline.
misconceptions: A work-report guarantee means the package data is already assured available by a validator super-majority.

relations.statement: A newly guaranteed report becomes the pending availability assignment for its core under protocol rules.

title: Work-report guarantee

canonical_fact: Guaranteeing is the off-chain validator process of obtaining package data, validating authorization and inputs, running Refine, distributing availability data and producing a signed work-report guarantee.
title: Guaranteeing

canonical_fact: A guarantee carries validator credentials that authenticate which guarantors signed the work report.
title: Guarantee credentials

canonical_fact: A guaranteed work report is associated with a particular core, whose authorization and availability state are updated by the report.
title: Core assignment

canonical_fact: A guarantee records the timeslot associated with reporting so protocol freshness and assignment rules can be checked.
title: Guarantee timeslot

canonical_fact: JAM requires the data behind a guaranteed work report to become available to validators before the report's implications can safely progress toward accumulation.
title: Data availability

canonical_fact: Per core, JAM tracks a guaranteed work report whose work-package availability still requires validator assurances.
title: Availability assignment

canonical_fact: An assurance is a validator statement indicating which pending work-package data the validator has correctly received and is storing locally.
misconceptions: An assurance is a vote on whether Refine computed the correct result.

relations.statement: Enough validator assurances cause a pending report to become available.

title: Availability assurance

canonical_fact: A work report becomes available only after the protocol observes the required super-majority of validator assurances for its data.
title: Availability threshold

canonical_fact: When a pending report first satisfies the availability condition, it enters the set of newly available reports considered by accumulation.

relations.statement: Newly available reports are candidates for accumulation, subject to dependencies and gas.

title: Newly available report

canonical_fact: Auditing re-executes selected reported work independently to detect incorrect work reports after guaranteeing.
misconceptions: Auditing is the same step as guaranteeing and is performed only by the original guarantors.

relations.statement: An audit can lead a validator to issue a judgment on report validity.

title: Audit

canonical_fact: Validators determine which work reports they are responsible for auditing according to protocol-defined assignment and randomness rules.
title: Audit selection

canonical_fact: Auditors fetch the auditable work-package representation so they can verify Refine without reconstructing all source data in the same costly way as guarantors.
title: Auditable data

canonical_fact: A judgment is a validator's signed conclusion about the validity of disputed or audited work, contributing to protocol agreement over whether a report is valid or invalid.
title: Judgment

canonical_fact: The disputes extrinsic carries information about validator disagreement over report validity and is used to update protocol judgment state.
misconceptions: A dispute is merely a temporary network fork and is unrelated to work-report validity.

relations.statement: Dispute processing can identify validator misbehavior and feed offender state.

title: Dispute

canonical_fact: Validators determined to have misbehaved can be marked as offenders, influencing later validator-set rotation and block-header offender markers.
title: Offender

canonical_fact: A report judged invalid must not be allowed to drive normal state evolution, and chain selection and finality rules avoid preserving extensions known to contain invalid reported data.
title: Invalid report effect

canonical_fact: JAM explicitly specifies off-chain honest behavior including guaranteeing, distributing availability data, assuring availability and auditing work reports.
title: Validator honest behavior

canonical_fact: Guarantors build and execute work reports before on-chain reporting, while auditors independently re-check selected reports afterward using auditable data; the roles provide separate correctness checks.
title: Audit versus guarantee
